correctness.rationale: On a spider, resistance distance is series resistance and the all-vertex maximum is the sum of the two largest arm resistances. Cauchy--Schwarz determines the unique least-price conductance profile for any specified arm resistance. In the resulting strictly convex budget-at-fixed-diameter problem, all but a largest arm resistance coincide; assigning the largest to the maximum arm price and minimizing a strictly convex scalar function gives the two exact branches. Attainment, boundary equality and uniqueness follow; 13,714 reproducible standalone exact/numeric checks and 20 independent epigraph objective comparisons agree.

value.rationale: The natural network fairness invariant is maximum pairwise electrical resistance. An exact arbitrary-arm-length and edge-price conductance design, with a sharp dominance transition depending on squared sums of sqrt prices (or squared lengths at equal prices), is directly usable and does not follow as a trivial rescaling of total-resistance design; general conic optimization alone does not expose the structural boundary.
